brief: GS Contessa's Monday close color for Oct 5. The tape closed broadly higher, S&P +66bps to 7,773, NDX +87bps, R2K +73bps, Dow +18bps, on volume below the YTD average. Brazil's election outcome, Bolsonaro 47.0% versus Lula 45.2%, was read as substantially better for the market than expected, driving EWZ up 13% as macro shorts got squeezed and hedge funds bought against long-only supply. Derivatives flow in EWZ chased short-dated call upside. Merger Monday added Schneider Electric's $22.6bn deal for PTX, C.H. Robinson's $5.8bn deal for RXO, and a reported McKesson and CD&R approach for an infusion-services provider that sent OPCH up 20% after hours. Desk activity was rated 4 of 10, with long-onlys light net sellers of macro and hedge funds light net buyers of tech. US long/short net leverage sits near five-year, 2nd-percentile lows, which the desk says sets up forced buying if the index extends higher. In derivatives, skew was crushed into the rally, a customer bought 20k Nov 19 VIX 17 put spreads, and the desk likes semis into earnings, flagging AMAT and CDNS call spreads, plus QQQ optionality. The S&P's implied move for the rest of the week is 90bps.
